explanation: A summer skort heading into winter: shoppers who buy it slumped at this time last year and recent weeks are cooling, so a steep drop was expected and happened.
This top sold far more last winter and fits back-to-school, so the model expected a strong rebound into autumn; it beat even that.
Brand-new shorts launching into summer were lifted for their partial first months and hot first weeks, but the launch took off even faster.

A heavy faux-fur coat moving into spring was expected to fall sharply on weather, shopper history and cooling sales, and fell further still, likely because holiday promotions had inflated its recent run rate.
Its own and its shoppers' history said this sweatshirt would slump deeply after winter, but it held up better, perhaps helped by clearance pricing.
A sweater past its winter peak, cooling fast and with holiday-boosted recent sales, was expected to drop by about 70% and did.
Denim shorts that sold strongly last summer and suit festival season were expected to climb into spring despite a weak shopper-cluster signal, and climbed even more.
A black lace tank with slightly warming sales and some Halloween fit was expected to stay near its run rate, but grew about 50%, more than any feature anticipated.
A brand-new mini dress heading into prom and party season was lifted for its short history, but sales exploded far beyond that, a launch hit the data could not foresee.
New low-rise denim shorts were expected to roughly hold their level into winter, but nearly doubled, suggesting the launch was still ramping or caught a trend.
A summery halter top got a late burst of sales that lifted the forecast, but heading into winter the burst faded and sales fell harder than expected.
A summer babydoll top already cooling, with weak shopper-cluster history, was forecast to dip modestly thanks to summer calendar lifts, but it fell much further.
An oversized tee with a hot recent month and autumn fit was forecast to grow 40%, but sales only held flat as the recent spike did not carry over.
New sunglasses heading out of summer were lifted mainly for their short history and still sold twice the forecast as the launch kept building.
A small-volume summer tank cooling into autumn was forecast to fall by about half and fell further, as end-of-season items often do.
This best-selling baggy jean always slumps after the holidays, by its own and its shoppers' history, so a big post-holiday drop was forecast and happened.
A cozy hoodie heading into winter got a strong lift for falling temperatures and a warming recent trend, and beat even that forecast.
Nylon shorts moving from summer into autumn were forecast to fall about 30%, but end-of-season demand dropped off faster than the model allowed.
A basic white tank cooling after summer was forecast to drop about a quarter, with its staple style limiting the fall, which matched.
A denim skort with hot recent sales and back-to-school appeal was held back by its product type and early history, but kept growing as a still-young item.
A small-volume necklace whose sales had already collapsed was forecast to halve but sold nothing at all, most likely because it was delisted or out of stock.
A white tailored shirt with an occasion coming up was forecast to dip slightly into autumn, but grew by more than a third, a lift the data did not show coming.
A statement party dress cooling in recent weeks was propped up by its party-season fit and warm-state customers, but faded faster than forecast.
Faux-leather pants heading into autumn, Halloween and party season were forecast to double, and nearly quadrupled as the look caught on even more.
A cozy sweater with hot recent sales was lifted for the coming cold, but post-holiday calendar effects offset that, leaving a small expected dip which matched.
A petite version of the best-selling baggy jean was cooling and heading out of jeans weather, so a drop was expected; it stalled a bit more than forecast.
Sequin party shorts past their holiday-party season were forecast to fall by about 60% as last year's pattern and cooling sales suggested, and they did.
A red lace-up corset coming off Halloween was forecast to halve on last year's pattern, and fell further as the costume demand that had inflated recent sales vanished.
Gold party micro shorts heading toward Halloween and the party season were forecast to grow strongly and beat that a little.
A knit sweater whose sales were already collapsing at winter's end was forecast to drop about 75%; it held up slightly better.
A faux-leather party top after the holidays was expected to fall by more than half, mainly on its shoppers' post-holiday slump, but held up somewhat better.
A satin party dress after the holiday season was forecast to fall about 45% on the usual post-holiday slump, and did exactly that.
A new yellow lace mini dress with hot early sales was lifted for its short history, but spring demand ran far beyond the forecast as the launch took off.
A graphic long-sleeve tee with a hot recent month and strong back-to-school fit was forecast to more than double, but the buzz faded and it grew only about a third.
White baggy jeans were lifted for the coming cold weather, offset by cooling recent sales and weak shopper history, landing near flat; they slipped about 10% instead.
A best-selling hoodie heading from summer into winter was forecast to more than double, and sales rose even faster, about three and a half times.
A best-selling baggy jean heading into back-to-school was forecast to grow by two-thirds, and grew slightly more.
A summer tank heading into autumn was expected to drop about 40% as summer sales fade and its shoppers' history slumped, and it did.
A satin party dress cooling after the holidays was forecast to fall by half, which matched.
A summer tank with warm recent weeks was forecast to dip modestly into autumn but fell further as summer demand ended.

Studded micro shorts going into autumn were forecast to fall about 40% on cooling weather, with a little Halloween lift, and fell slightly less.
A red lace cami cooling in recent weeks got some lift for the upcoming party season but fell much further than forecast.
Low-volume summer micro shorts got a boost from strong shopper-cluster history, but demand fell away into autumn far faster than forecast.
A new wrap sweater with hot early sales was lifted for its short history against the post-holiday slump, and took off much faster still.
A hoodie with hot recent sales heading into winter was held near flat by post-holiday calendar effects, but sold about a third more than its run rate.
Waffle micro shorts with collapsing winter sales and a weak history for these months were forecast to fall sharply, but spring demand held up better.
Knit shorts cooling in recent weeks were forecast to drop by about a third despite summer approaching, and they did.
An oversized denim jacket heading into back-to-school and jacket weather was forecast to grow 70%, and grew even more.
A leopard scarf selling little in summer was forecast to double into winter on cold weather and rising sales, but it took off nearly twentyfold, more like a trend hit.
White linen pants were forecast to fall 35% on their shoppers' post-holiday slump, but held level as spring demand for linen arrived early.
A faux-leather belt was forecast to grow into winter on its accessory type and seasonal fit, but sales fell by a third instead, as if stock or demand dried up.
Young sweatpants were forecast to fall sharply on the post-holiday calendar, but kept selling near their run rate as the item was still building.
A summer tank in winter got a lift from its strong sales half a year ago, which overstated spring demand, and it fell more than forecast.
A small-volume studded skort heading into spring was forecast to hold its level on summer-weather fit, but grew by more than half.
A tiny-volume summer knit top was forecast to fall by about a third into autumn, but sold only a handful of units, a big miss in log terms but small in units.
A graphic tee that sold well last winter was forecast to double on back-to-school and summer calendar lifts, but grew only about a third.
A sheer lace top was forecast to edge up through summer, but sales fell 40%, a decline nothing in its history flagged.
A satin party dress cooling after winter was forecast to fall about 40%, but spring party demand kept it a little stronger.
A statement sequin poncho cooling fast after its launch was forecast to fall about a third and fell slightly more.
A cozy waffle top was forecast to drop by two-thirds on its own and its shoppers' post-holiday history, but the slump was a bit milder.
A new lacy babydoll top was lifted for its short history and the party season, but sales grew elevenfold, a breakout launch far beyond any forecast.
A summery crochet mini dress with hot recent sales was forecast to grow slightly through winter, but it tripled, more like a trend hit than a seasonal pattern.
A graphic hoodie after the holidays was forecast to fall by more than half on its own and its shoppers' history, and fell a little further.

The same graphic tee was again forecast to more than double on back-to-school fit and hot recent sales, and again grew only about a third.
A striped summer tank cooling into autumn was forecast to drop about a third and dropped a bit more as summer demand ended.
This tank's sales had dropped sharply in the last month, so a big fall was forecast, but sales rebounded strongly, consistent with a restock after a stock-out.
A lacey top that sold much more last winter, with rising recent sales and buoyant shopper-cluster history, was forecast to more than double and nearly did.
A long-sleeve tee heading into colder months was lifted by the weather but held back by cooling recent sales, and sold a bit more than forecast.
A small-volume jean that always slumps into spring, by its own and its shoppers' history, was forecast to drop about 65% and did.
A brand-new striped sweater launched into autumn was forecast to grow sevenfold on cold weather and its short history, but became a breakout hit selling about seventy times its early run rate.
A satin party dress, warm in recent weeks before the holidays, was forecast to fall about 40% over winter on its shoppers' seasonal slump, which matched.
A satin-and-lace corset with warming recent sales was forecast to grow slightly through summer and early autumn, and did.
Wide-leg pants with a hot recent month were held back by post-holiday calendar and shopper-cluster effects, giving a small expected dip that matched.
Summer ruffle shorts heading into winter were forecast to fall by about 60% on their own and their shoppers' history, and did.
A summery chiffon top cooling into autumn was forecast to drop over 60%, but held up somewhat better, possibly helped by end-of-season pricing.
A small embroidered sweater was forecast to nearly double into back-to-school and autumn, and instead nearly quadrupled.
Best-selling denim shorts heading into festival season and summer, with hot recent sales, were forecast to double and grew even more.
A seashell graphic tee was propped up by back-to-school fit and forecast to hold steady, but sales fell by more than half as its summer moment passed.
A young studded tank was marked down sharply because its co-purchase neighbours slumped last spring, but it grew by a quarter as summer approached.
A denim skort whose winter sales had cooled was forecast to fall by half, but spring demand brought it right back to its run rate.
Wide-leg foldover pants with a strong recent surge were held back by post-holiday calendar and shopper-cluster effects, leaving a small expected dip that matched.
A cable-knit sweater collapsing after winter was forecast to fall about 75% and fell even further as its season ended.
Ribbed knit sweatpants heading into back-to-school and cooler months were forecast to grow 75%, but more than tripled.
An off-shoulder knit top was forecast to grow into winter on cold-weather fit and strong shopper history, but sales halved, consistent with stock running out or the trend fading.
A beaded party dress cooling after winter was forecast to dip about a quarter, softened by spring weather, and held up about as expected.
A backless knit party dress with hot recent sales and strong shopper-cluster history was forecast to grow a third into prom season and grew about a fifth.
A satin party dress with warming sales and an occasion coming soon was forecast to grow about 20% into autumn, and did.
An off-shoulder knit mini dress past its winter season was forecast to drop two-thirds on its own and its shoppers' history, with a small Valentine's lift, and did.
Best-selling white baggy jeans heading into back-to-school with warming sales were forecast to grow about 50% and grew a little less.
A beaded statement dress with a hot recent month was forecast to hold its level, but the buzz faded and sales fell by a third.
A faux-leather corset coming off Halloween and holiday parties was forecast to fall by more than half, and fell exactly that much.
French-terry sweatpants heading into winter were lifted by the cold-weather turn and forecast to grow about a quarter, which matched.
A sequin poncho with holiday-party fit and warm-state customers was forecast to stay near its run rate through winter, and it did.
Young bootcut jeans cooling into spring, sold to customers in colder states and with weak shopper-cluster history, were forecast to halve and roughly did.
A polka-dot tee was forecast to fall 45% on the post-holiday calendar, but held its run rate as spring tee demand came in strongly.
A babydoll top whose sales collapsed in the last month was forecast to drop by two-thirds, but lost only a third, as if a stock gap had depressed the recent weeks.
A party top with hot holiday-season sales was forecast to drop about 30% after the holidays on its shoppers' history, and dropped slightly more.
A long-running white mini skirt with an occasion coming up was forecast to dip slightly into autumn, but grew about 10%.
A tiny-volume lace top was forecast to fall 60% on weak shopper and own history, but sold close to its run rate, a gap of only a few units.

Studded micro shorts heading into winter were forecast to fall by nearly half on colder weather and cooling sales, and fell slightly less.

A lacy party dress heading into the holidays was forecast to fall about a third over winter as its shoppers slump, and did.
A striped henley tank with hot recent sales was held back by its weak early history, and kept growing about 30% as a rising item.

Studded faux-suede shorts with hot recent sales and strong Halloween fit were forecast to grow about a third into autumn and grew a little less.
A new sheer poncho with hot recent sales and holiday-party fit was pulled down by winter calendar effects, but kept growing strongly as a young item.
Striped summer shorts were forecast to fall 45% over winter, but held their run rate as spring shorts demand arrived and the young item kept building.
A young button-up tank heading into summer was forecast to edge up slightly, held back by its short early history, and grew about 20%.
Nylon shorts whose sales dipped over the holidays were forecast to halve, but spring demand brought them back to their run rate.
A tiny-volume strapless knit top with cooling sales was forecast to slip about a quarter through summer, and did.
A green party top heading into spring and prom season was forecast to dip slightly on its shoppers' history, but grew about 15%.
